No. According to [[write-journal]], it does **not** use a database transaction. The page explicitly states:

> "This provides all-or-nothing semantics for writes without needing a database transaction—the in-memory journal itself acts as a transaction log for the duration of a single run."

So the rollback mechanism is implemented through the in-memory write journal itself, which tracks prior file state and can reverse writes by restoring previous content or deleting newly created files—all within the lifetime of a single agent run, without any database transaction layer.
